nodes.name: Electrochemical Activation and Oxyanion Engineering
nodes.procedure: A two-electrode system using NiFe-LDH as model anode is employed to simulate conditions at 80 °C. K3PO4 was introduced as an electrolyte additive. To fully activate the NiFe-LDH anodes, 20-hour chronopotentiometry (CP) tests were conducted at 80 °C and 400 mA cm-2.

unit_operations.name: Electrolyte Preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: K3PO4 was introduced as an electrolyte additive

unit_operations.name: Chronopotentiometry Activation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: we conducted 20-hour CP tests at 80 °C and 400 mA cm-2 to fully activate the NiFe-LDH anodes.

nodes.source_text: A two-electrode system using NiFe-LDH as model anode ... to fully activate the NiFe-LDH anodes.

nodes.name: Drip-coating Modification
nodes.procedure: drip-coating PO4 on the catalyst surface or by preparing NiFe-LDH containing PO4
nodes.source_text: the stability of the catalysts can also be improve by drip-coating PO4 on the catalyst surface

nodes.name: Industrial Electrolyzer Assembly
nodes.procedure: An industrial-grade electrolyzer comprising 10 cells has been assembled based on NiFe-LDH anodes with radii of 59 mm. Raney Ni coated nickel mesh were used as the cathodes, and AGFA Zirfon UTP500 as the membranes. The electrolyte was 20 wt% KOH with 10 mM K3PO4.
nodes.source_text: an industrial-grade electrolyzer comprising 10 cells has been assembled based on NiFe-LDH anodes with radii of 59 mm... AGFA Zirfon UTP500 as the membranes... with 10 mM phosphate ion introduction.

nodes.name: Control Electrochemical Activation
nodes.procedure: A two-electrode system using NiFe-LDH as anode and Pt foil as cathode was operated at 80 °C under 400 mA cm-2 for 20 hours in a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte without inhibitors.
nodes.source_text: The performance variation is assessed via the chronopotentiometry (CP) test... the rate of voltage degradation reaches 18 mV/h within just 20 hours at elevated temperatures.

nodes.description: Stability test at room temperature (rt) in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Conversely, no significant voltage change is observed at rt., indicating the stability of NiFe-LDH is a serious issue when operating at industry-relevant condition.

nodes.description: Baseline OER stability and activity test at 80 °C (No inhibitor)
nodes.source_text: the rate of voltage degradation reaches 18 mV / h... overpotential required to achieve 10 mAcm−2 increases by 40 mV (η10 = 251 mV)... required 0.35 V vs Hg / HgO to initiate the electrooxidation and commenced OER at 0.37 V vs Hg / HgO... redeposition of dissolved Ni and Fe (7.08 ppm Ni2+ and 6.25 ppm Fe3+) from NiFe-LDH anode.

nodes.description: OER performance and kinetics at 80 °C with 10 mM K3PO4
nodes.source_text: achieving a current density of 10 mA cm−2 at approximately 0.376 V vs Hg / HgO... middle-frequency region at 0.33 V vs Hg / HgO diminishes rapidly, indicating the electrooxidation... onset of oxygen production around 0.35 V vs Hg / HgO... amount of adsorbed PO43− on the electrode surface falls below the detection limit.

nodes.description: Optimized long-term OER stability with phosphate and Ni foam cathode
nodes.source_text: operated stably at 400 mA cm−2 for 100 h with a degradation rate of 0.72 mV / h... nodes.source_text: After the concentration of K3PO4 reached 100 mM... onset potential of NiFe-LDH did not undergo significant changes, the rate of current growth decreased a lot... adsorbed amount of PO43− increased to 15.5 ppm.
